basic_details.scholarship_name: Rotary Peace Fellowship (Duke University & UNC Chapel Hill Peace Center)
basic_details.offering_entity: The Rotary Foundation of Rotary International & Duke-UNC Rotary Peace Center
basic_details.host_institutions_covered: Duke University (Sanford School of Public Policy) & University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (Chapel Hill, North Carolina, USA)
degree_levels: Master of Arts (MA in Global Studies, Political Science, or Public Health)
basic_details.major_restrictions: International Development Policy, Peace and Conflict Resolution, Global Health Policy, Environmental Policy & Peacebuilding, Human Rights & Humanitarian Assistance, and International Security.
basic_details.number_of_awards_total: ~130 fully funded Rotary Peace Fellowships awarded globally per year across all Rotary Peace Centers
basic_details.number_of_awards_pakistan: Open globally on merit; Pakistani peace practitioners, development leaders, and policy analysts regularly win competitive fellowship slots (~4 to 8 awards globally)
basic_details.duration_of_scholarship: Up to 24 months (Two full academic years, including a 2 to 3-month Applied Field Experience internship)
basic_details.monthly_stipend_amount: $2,200 to $2,600 / month living stipend (~PKR 610,000 to 720,000 / month) plus 100% full tuition, round-trip international airfare, health insurance, and fully funded field internship

nationality_requirements: Open to citizens of all countries including Pakistan (Rotarians and immediate family members ineligible)
eligibility_requirements.age_limit_notes: No age restriction; candidates must demonstrate substantial professional peace, conflict, or development track records.
eligibility_requirements.academic_qualifications: Recognized 16-year Bachelor's degree with strong academic record (equivalent to minimum GPA 3.00 / 4.00 or second-division upper / 65%+) from an HEC-recognized university.
eligibility_requirements.grading_conversion_notes: Minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 / 4.0; selection heavily emphasizes professional peacebuilding impact and leadership capacity.
eligibility_requirements.subject_background_prerequisites: Social sciences, law, development studies, international relations, environmental studies, or related disciplines.
eligibility_requirements.current_education_status: Graduated professionals with active employment in peacebuilding, development, or humanitarian sectors.
eligibility_requirements.graduation_year_restrictions: Must have completed bachelor's degree at least 3 years prior to fellowship start date.
eligibility_requirements.work_experience_notes: Minimum 3 years of full-time relevant professional work experience in peacebuilding, human rights, conflict mitigation, or sustainable development.
eligibility_requirements.language_notes: IELTS Academic minimum 7.0 or TOEFL iBT minimum 90 mandatory for Duke University Sanford School and UNC Chapel Hill admissions.
eligibility_requirements.other_language_requirements: Second language proficiency recommended but not mandatory.
eligibility_requirements.special_eligibility_categories: Candidates must obtain endorsement from a local Rotary District; active Rotarians, Rotary club members, or their lineal descendants are barred by Rotary Foundation bylaws.
eligibility_requirements.previous_scholarship_restrictions: Ineligible if already awarded a Rotary Peace Fellowship.

tuition_fee.details: 100% full international tuition, mandatory registration fees, and academic course charges at Duke University and UNC Chapel Hill.

admission_application_fee.details: Rotary Peace Fellowship application is free; host university graduate application fees are waived or reimbursed by Rotary.

accommodation.details: Housing allowance provided via monthly living stipend; fellows lease private apartments or university graduate housing in Durham / Chapel Hill.

monthly_stipend.details: Monthly tax-free living stipend of $2,200 to $2,600 / month directly deposited to cover rent, utilities, food, and living expenses.

airfare.details: Round-trip economy international airfare between Pakistan and Raleigh-Durham International Airport (RDU), North Carolina.

visa_fee.details: U.S. J-1 Exchange Visitor Visa or F-1 Student Visa application fees and SEVIS fees covered or reimbursed by the fellowship.

health_insurance.details: Comprehensive student health and hospitalization insurance policy through Duke University or UNC Chapel Hill student health services.

food_allowance.details: Dining and grocery costs covered through monthly living allowance.

books_and_materials_allowance.details: Annual textbook and course materials allowance provided at the start of each academic semester.

research_funding_conference_grant.details: Fully funded 2 to 3-month summer Applied Field Experience (AFE) internship including international travel, living allowance, and project grant up to $6,000 to $8,000.

travel_transit_allowance.details: Local GoTriangle and Duke Robertson bus transit passes included, providing free connectivity between Duke and UNC campuses.

university_and_program_options.single_or_multiple_universities: Dual elite host universities forming the joint Duke-UNC Rotary Peace Center.
participating_institutions: Duke University (Sanford School of Public Policy, Durham, North Carolina, USA)
University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (College of Arts and Sciences, Chapel Hill, North Carolina, USA)
university_and_program_options.university_rankings_scope: Duke University ranked #10 in U.S. News & World Report and Top 25 globally; UNC Chapel Hill ranked #4 among U.S. public universities; Sanford School of Public Policy ranked Top 5 in public policy.
available_majors: Master of International Development Policy (MIDP at Duke Sanford)
Master of Arts in Global Studies (UNC Chapel Hill)
Master of Public Policy (MPP in Peacebuilding & Conflict Transformation)
Master of Science in Public Health (Global Health Policy at Gillings)
Master of Environmental Management (Peace & Resource Governance at Duke Nicholas)
university_and_program_options.program_duration: 24 months (2 academic years + summer Applied Field Experience)
university_and_program_options.admission_requirements_summary: Bachelor's degree with 3.0+ GPA, minimum 3 years full-time peace/development work experience, Rotary District endorsement, IELTS 7.0+ or TOEFL 90+, essays on peace vision, two recommendation letters, and CV.
university_and_program_options.easiest_hardest_institutions_guidance: Selection is conducted in two stages: Rotary Foundation first selects Peace Fellows; fellows then apply to Duke University or UNC Chapel Hill graduate school with guaranteed funding endorsement.
university_and_program_options.strategic_program_match_advice: Focus personal essays on tangible grassroots or policy achievements in conflict mitigation, refugee protection, human rights, or environmental justice in South Asia.

application_process_roadmap.portal_system_name: Rotary Foundation Online Peace Fellowship Application Portal (Embark)
application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Create an account on the Rotary Peace Fellowships portal, select Master's program track, list Duke-UNC as preferred Peace Center, draft peace essays, upload transcripts and CV, and request endorsement from local Rotary District.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Check eligibility (3+ years relevant work experience, not an active Rotarian or lineal relative).
Step 2: Connect with local Rotary District in Pakistan (District 3271 or 3272) to request interview and district endorsement.
Step 3: Complete online Rotary Peace Fellowship application including peace leadership essays and CV.
Step 4: Referees submit letters of recommendation directly into the portal by May 15.
Step 5: Rotary District conducts interview and submits endorsement to The Rotary Foundation by July 1.
Step 6: World-level Rotary Selection Committee reviews dossiers and announces fellowship awards in November.
Step 7: Selected fellows submit formal graduate admission application to Duke University or UNC Chapel Hill by December/January.
Step 8: Universities issue formal admission letters; Rotary processes visa, travel, and stipend for August departure.
application_process_roadmap.university_vs_scholarship_routing: Two-Stage Coordinated Track: Candidates win the Rotary Peace Fellowship first, followed by streamlined formal admission to Duke or UNC Chapel Hill.
application_process_roadmap.recommendation_letters_submission_method: Submitted online by referees via automated secure electronic appraisal forms.
application_process_roadmap.personal_statement_prompts: Essays detailing: (1) Professional experience in peace and development, (2) Motivation for pursuing the fellowship, (3) Theory of change and concrete vision for advancing peace in Pakistan/globally.
application_process_roadmap.study_plan_research_proposal_requirement: Statement of academic and professional objectives outlining intended coursework and ideas for the Applied Field Experience internship.
application_process_roadmap.cv_format_requirements: Chronological professional CV highlighting employment history, peacebuilding initiatives, publications, and volunteer leadership.
application_process_roadmap.interview_format_details: District endorsement interview with senior Rotary leaders, followed by potential virtual interview with host university faculty.
application_process_roadmap.standardized_tests: IELTS Academic 7.0+ or TOEFL iBT 90+ mandatory; GRE optional.
application_process_roadmap.attestation_requirements: HEC verified transcripts required upon formal university enrollment.
application_process_roadmap.translation_requirements: Certified English translation of all non-English documents.
application_process_roadmap.final_submission_method: 100% online submission via Rotary Foundation Embark portal.

important_dates_timeline.application_deadline: May 15 (Annual candidate submission deadline to Rotary Foundation)
important_dates_timeline.annual_cycle_notes: Single annual cycle: Submit by May 15, 2026 for fellowship commencement in August 2027.

selection_process_and_weights.extracurricular_and_leadership_weight: 35% (Proven track record in peace, conflict resolution, social justice, or humanitarian work)
selection_process_and_weights.research_experience_weight: 10% (Policy papers, analytical writing, or field assessment experience)
selection_process_and_weights.work_experience_weight: 25% (Minimum 3 years of high-impact full-time professional experience)
selection_process_and_weights.selection_panel_composition: Rotary Foundation International Selection Committee comprising Global Trustees and Peace Experts, in consultation with Duke-UNC Academic Directors.
selection_process_and_weights.evaluation_methodology: Holistic global competition evaluating candidate's dedication to peacebuilding, leadership accomplishments, and capacity to leverage the fellowship for global impact.

competitiveness_profile.total_annual_applicants: ~1,500 to 2,500 global peace practitioners applying across all peace centers
competitiveness_profile.total_scholarships_awarded: ~50 master's fellowships globally; ~10 to 12 fellows at Duke-UNC center annually
competitiveness_profile.acceptance_rate_pakistan: ~2.5% to 4.0% for distinguished peace practitioners with district endorsement
competitiveness_profile.typical_successful_applicant_gpa: Undergraduate GPA >= 3.40 / 4.00, accompanied by 4 to 8 years of distinguished peacebuilding, NGO, or humanitarian experience
competitiveness_profile.typical_academic_and_research_profile: Mid-level practitioners in international NGOs (UN, ICRC, USAID, Oxfam), human rights lawyers, investigative journalists, and government development officers.
competitiveness_profile.common_backgrounds_of_winners: Pakistani alumni from leading universities (LUMS, Quaid-i-Azam, NUST, Kinnaird, IBA) working in development, gender rights, and community peacebuilding.
competitiveness_profile.high_representation_countries: Pakistan, USA, Colombia, Kenya, India, Nigeria, UK, Myanmar, Syria, Uganda.

fake_websites_and_scams: Only apply through official Rotary portal at rotary.org.
Rotary International never charges fees for applications or district endorsements.
red_flags_and_warnings.application_fee_warning: The fellowship application is 100% free of charge.
red_flags_and_warnings.agent_and_intermediary_warnings: Commercial agencies cannot secure Rotary endorsements; candidates must connect directly with local Rotary clubs and districts.
hidden_costs_breakdown: All primary expenses (tuition, flights, housing, stipend, health, AFE grant) are 100% covered.
Domestic travel to Rotary club/district meetings for interview: ~PKR 10,000 to 20,000.
IELTS or TOEFL test registration: ~PKR 55,000 to 65,000.
misleading_claims_debunked: Myth: You must be a Rotarian to apply. Reality: Rotarians and their immediate relatives are legally barred from receiving Rotary Peace Fellowships to avoid conflict of interest.
Myth: The fellowship only covers short certificates. Reality: The Master's track covers a full two-year elite master's degree (Duke MIDP or UNC MA) with generous funding.
official_vs_unofficial_discrepancies: Unofficial sites post inaccurate deadlines; official Rotary Foundation portal deadline is strictly May 15 annually.

scholarship_obligations_and_terms.minimum_gpa_maintenance: Must maintain a minimum cumulative graduate GPA of 3.0 / 4.0 throughout each semester at Duke and UNC.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.attendance_requirements: Full-time resident study in North Carolina and completion of the mandatory 2 to 3-month Applied Field Experience.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.academic_progress_monitoring: Biannual academic progress evaluation and reporting to The Rotary Foundation.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.work_restrictions_during_study: Scholars are discouraged from outside paid work to ensure full engagement with coursework and peace center activities.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.home_country_return_obligation: None; fellows become lifelong Rotary Peace Fellows and can pursue global peace careers with international organizations or return to home country.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.service_obligations_or_bonds: Obligation to present research at the annual Duke-UNC Rotary Peace Conference and submit post-fellowship career reports.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.repayment_clawback_conditions: Funding terminated if fellow withdraws or fails academic good standing.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.rules_for_changing_major: Permitted only within approved peace and development degree programs at Duke and UNC.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.extension_policy: Funding capped strictly at 24 months; no extensions permitted.
